_comment: Default watchlist for the toolsmith PreToolUse redirect hook. Each 'pattern' is a JavaScript RegExp (tested against the raw Bash command string). A watched command is only ever DENIED when an approved registry tool's 'covers' pattern also matches it; a watched command with no covering tool passes through to the normal permission flow. Projects override this set via .claude/toolsmith/config.json ({"watchlist": {"add": [...], "remove": [...]}}); 'remove' entries must match a pattern string here verbatim.

watchlist.rationale: gh api makes arbitrary authenticated REST calls with the CLI's full credentials — the classic broad escape hatch. Narrow read operations belong in a purpose-built, allowlistable script.
gh graphql runs arbitrary authenticated GraphQL against GitHub — same broad-power concern as gh api.
curl to a non-local host is an unbounded network fetch/post. Recurring API reads should become a scoped script rather than a hand-rolled request.
wget to a non-local host is an unbounded network fetch — same concern as curl.
The raw aws CLI spans every AWS service and mutation. A specific recurring query should be a bounded script, not a broadly allowlisted aws command.
The raw gcloud CLI spans all of Google Cloud. Narrow recurring operations should be scripted and scoped.
kubectl can read and mutate any cluster resource. Recurring inspections should be captured as read-only scoped scripts.
The 1Password CLI reads secrets. Any recurring secret access should be a single, reviewed, tightly-scoped script rather than an allowlisted op command.
